chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: Reactions to Beneath the Underdog and Louis Lomax
summary: Names he used, fear of some characters, and how the manuscript was copied and spread.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Book's been out awhile now. It's in paperback as well, so I wondered --
My book?
Yeah, I saw a paperback version somewhere. I wonder if you've gotten any reactions from people on the book? What kind of reactions you got, anyway.
Oh, well, father loves it.
Yeah.
(Inaudible) McGee I use his name. All those guys told me I could use their names.
Yeah.
But Mel King I scared. All else he didn't believe me. I was talking about Bennie Bell, too.
Yeah.
Everybody was afraid to use his name.
If you were going to do another book, what would it be on?
I'd try and clear that one up.
Yeah, like, for example?

Well, see, when I was writing that book, and give it to Louis Lomax, I expected him to take the names out like I hired him to do. And all the people would have laughed at themselves, that I wrote about.
Yeah.

That's why I wrote the book. So (inaudible) I'd clear the book up. To write a book where I tell everybody what they're doing, but with different names, and so personal that they'd laugh and say, oh, Mingus is talking about me here, and only me would know it, you know?
Yeah.
But the original copy got out in a whole lot of hands. I give it to you, --
Yeah.
-- and somebody would copy it. There's a guy named Bunch, owns a soul food restaurant in the East Village called Bunche's.
Don't know him.
Well, his wife work for the CIA, and she said the CIA had it.
